title: Building networks, fostering innovation: Designing and facilitating a collaborative faculty mentor training program
journal: To Improve the Academy: A Journal of Educational Development
abstract: This article examines a faculty mentor training program developed to support a university-wide transition to a new learning management system (LMS). Rather than treating the transition as a purely technical challenge, the program leveraged institutional change to engage faculty in collaborative, peer-led professional learning. Framed within literature on faculty mentoring and educational change, the program emphasized co-construction, experiential training, and mentor agency to prepare faculty mentors as instructional leaders and change agents. The eight-week, hybrid-format training engaged participants across academic units in discussions and LMS-building activities centered on course design, student engagement, assessment and feedback, and inclusive pedagogy. Activities were designed with ongoing participant input, and faculty mentors were active contributors to the program’s evolution—helping shape weekly content, mentoring strategies, and the broader vision for instructional support. A central aim was to find organic moments within the LMS transition to introduce pedagogical topics and prepare mentors to do the same with the instructors they would support. As program facilitators, we modeled best practices in teaching and mentorship while cultivating a feedback-driven learning environment. Participant feedback highlighted the value of co-construction, hands-on learning, collegial support, and clear expectations—but also revealed challenges around role clarity and workload sustainability. This experience suggests that peer-based educational development programs, when designed with flexibility, structure, and community in mind, can strengthen institutional capacity for pedagogical innovation. The article concludes with recommendations for institutions launching similar programs during times of institutional change, focusing on scaffolding mentor roles, supporting diverse expertise, and fostering long-term professional networks.

title: Why are tourists willing to wait longer in theme parks? The positive effects of narratives and destination brand love
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: Purpose This study examines why tourists are willing to incur additional waiting time for a preferred theme park experience rather than choose comparable alternatives involving shorter waits. Design/methodology/approach Zootopia at Shanghai Disneyland was selected as the research context. Study 1 used an online pretravel survey of tourists who had watched the film Zootopia (N = 247). Study 2 used an on-site survey of Zootopia themed land visitors (N = 278). The hypotheses were tested using PLS-SEM. Findings Study 1 shows that film narratives and destination brand love positively affect willingness to wait longer, while scene replication degree strengthens the effect of film narratives. Study 2 shows that film narratives directly increase willingness to wait longer and that destination brand love operates indirectly through flow experience. In Study 2, flow experience mediates the effects of film narratives and destination brand love, while scene replication degree strengthens the effect of film narratives. Practical implications Theme parks should leverage film narratives, strengthen scene replication, cultivate pretravel brand love, and enhance on-site experiences and provide safe, unobstructed queue environments. Originality/value This study advances understanding of tourists' willingness to wait longer in movie-themed theme parks by examining its relationships with film narratives and destination brand love. It further examines the mediating role of on-site flow experience and the moderating role of scene replication degree.

title: What is socially effective behavior? Unpacking the missing link in the social competence literature
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to identify social performance behaviors and their outcomes, avoiding conflation with other concepts such as personality traits or skills. This study provides theoretical insight into how and why social performance behaviors lead to social effectiveness outcomes. Design/methodology/approach This study involved interviewing and conducting focus groups with 44 participants. Grounded theory methodology was used to analyze the qualitative data produced from participants. Findings Analysis of participants’ responses revealed three categories of social performance behaviors: conversation behaviors, nonverbal communication behaviors, and networking behaviors. The study identified proximal and distal social effectiveness outcomes and clearly separated them from social performance behaviors to avoid conceptual conflation. The authors created a conceptual model explaining how and why social performance behaviors lead to various outcomes, enhancing understanding of the causal links between social behaviors and interpersonal results. Research limitations/implications A limitation of this study is that the conceptual model could not capture all social performance behaviors and outcomes. Future research should test the linkages proposed in the model and consider contextual factors. Practical implications This study identifies specific behaviors that can create desired interpersonal outcomes in the work environment. Training can be developed to teach individuals how to use these social performance behaviors, and behavioral flexibility can be encouraged. Originality/value This study represents an initial step towards comprehensive theory building within the social competence domain. This study both identifies important social performance behaviors and outcomes and explains how and why they are connected.

title: Trajectories of anxiety and depression levels in older adult patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty
abstract: BACKGROUND Total hip arthroplasty (THA) has become a core means of joint function enhancement among older adult patients due to global population aging. However, postoperative anxiety and depression compromise patients’ rehabilitation and quality of life. AIM To explore anxiety/depression trajectories among older adults who have undergone THA, identify high-risk factors, and propose stratified precision nursing strategies. METHODS This observational study enrolled 208 older adult patients who had undergone their first unilateral THA between June 2023 and June 2025. The Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale and Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression-17 items assessed anxiety and depression, respectively, combined with the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES), and Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). A latent category growth model was used to identify anxiety/depression subgroups, and multiple logistic regression was used to analyze the independent influencing factors. RESULTS Based on the dynamic trajectory of the patients’ anxiety and depression levels, which exhibited a “peaking at 1-week post-operation—gradual relief over the next 1 month”, patients were divided into two subgroups: The stable (42.79%; mild preoperative abnormalities and postoperative recovery after short-term fluctuations) and unstable group (57.21%; patient had moderate-to-severe negative emotions before surgery, which were relieved within three months). Old age (OR = 1.493), low education level (OR = 3.440), 1-week postoperative VAS (OR = 1.916), SSRS (OR = 0.894), and GSES (OR = 0.912) were independent factors for the high-risk group. CONCLUSION This study reveals the anxiety/depression heterogeneity among older adults who have undergone THA and suggests that the 1-week to 1-month post-operation is the key psychological intervention window.

title: Tinjauan Yuridis Keabsahan Surat Perjanjian Subkontrak di Bawah Tangan Dalam Pengadaan Barang/Jasa oleh Pelaku Ekonomi Kreatif
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis keabsahan hukum surat perjanjian subkontrak yang dibuat di bawah tangan oleh pelaku ekonomi kreatif dengan pemerintah dalam pengadaan barang/jasa serta menilai efektivitasnya dalam memberikan perlindungan hukum apabila terjadi sengketa. Latar belakang penelitian ini didasarkan pada maraknya praktik subkontrak oleh pelaku UMKM dan ekonomi kreatif yang seringkali tidak menggunakan akta autentik karena keterbatasan akses terhadap layanan notaris maupun pemahaman hukum kontrak. Padahal, lemahnya dokumen di bawah tangan menyebabkan posisi hukum pelaku usaha kecil menjadi rentan terhadap wanprestasi, kesulitan pembuktian di pengadilan, dan kerugian hukum lainnya. Urgensi penulisan ini terletak pada pentingnya membangun kesadaran hukum serta memberikan solusi konkret bagi pelaku ekonomi kreatif agar tetap terlindungi secara hukum dalam praktik subkontrak. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif-analitis, mengkaji ketentuan dalam KUHPerdata serta peraturan perundang-undangan terkait pengadaan dan kemitraan. Kebaruan dari penelitian ini terletak pada fokusnya terhadap praktik perjanjian subkontrak non-notariil dalam sektor swasta, khususnya oleh pelaku ekonomi kreatif, yang selama ini belum banyak dikaji secara mendalam. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa meskipun sah menurut hukum, surat perjanjian di bawah tangan memiliki kelemahan dalam aspek pembuktian dan perlindungan hukum, sehingga perlu upaya preventif melalui legalisasi atau penggunaan akta autentik berdasarkan persetujuan PPK, serta peningkatan literasi hukum di kalangan pelaku usaha kreatif untuk memperkuat posisi hukumnya dalam hubungan kontraktual.

title: Time-optimal trajectory planning based on dynamic constraints for a handling robot with kinematic redundancy
journal: Industrial Robot: the international journal of robotics research and application
abstract: Purpose This paper proposes a time-optimal trajectory planning method for high-speed and heavy-load handling robots with kinematic redundancy, aimed at significantly increasing the efficiency of stamping production lines. Design/methodology/approach Kinematic and dynamic models of the robot are established using the modified Denavit−Hartenberg method and the recursive Newton−Euler algorithm. A dynamics-aware constraint space is then constructed by incorporating controllable transient torque exceedance within predefined safety windows. In addition, a segmented trajectory accuracy regulation strategy is introduced to assign strict or relaxed path-error bounds according to operational phases. Finally, Genetic Algorithms-Sequential Quadratic Programming (GA-SQP) is adopted as a numerical solver to search for the minimum-time feasible trajectory under the coupled kinematic and dynamic constraints. Findings Physical experiments on the heavy-load robot platform validate that the optimized trajectory can be executed at 22 SPM. Compared with the original 18 SPM condition, the proposed method improves the production cycle rate while satisfying the predefined dynamic constraints. The measured torque responses are consistent with the simulation results, confirming the feasibility and safety of the proposed planning framework. Originality/value This study integrates task-level kinematic redundancy, segmented trajectory accuracy regulation and controllable dynamic overload constraints into a unified time-optimal planning model for high-speed heavy-load handling robots. Within this integrated framework, B-spline parameterization and a GA-SQP-based solution strategy with diversity-based initial point screening are used to obtain a minimum-time feasible trajectory while balancing efficiency, accuracy and dynamic safety.

title: The personalisation engine: converting customer-perceived organisational resources into customer experience and brand equity in fast-food restaurants
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how technological perception and customer centricity, as organisational resources, drive personalisation in fast-food restaurants. Grounded in service-dominant (S-D) logic and value co-creation, it also examines the moderating role of customer-perceived relevance as a situational trigger and evaluates the impact of personalisation on customer experience and brand equity. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted with 414 fast-food consumers. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The model demonstrated strong predictive power, explaining 75.5% of the variance in personalisation and highlighting it as a driver of customer experience and brand equity. Customer-perceived relevance also significantly moderated the relationship between technological perception and personalisation, acting as an attention filter that enhances technology's effectiveness. Originality/value This study fills a critical gap by examining personalisation in a utility-driven, standardised sector such as fast-food restaurants, where the balance between operational efficiency and tailored experiences poses a unique strategic challenge.

title: The association between work-life integration, job satisfaction, job stress, and innovative work behavior
journal: Journal of International Economics and Management
abstract: Purpose The study investigates the association between work-life integration and innovative work behavior, while examining job stress and job satisfaction as mediating variables. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted among employees from various industries. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The study was grounded in the Work-Home Resources model, Job Demands-Resources model, and Affective Events Theory. Findings The findings disclose a network of negative correlations, indicating that poor work-life integration is associated with higher stress and lower job satisfaction, which are linked to impaired innovation. Practical implications It contributes a higher-resolution, multidimensional understanding of how affective and cognitive strains undermine the innovation in collectivist work environments. Originality/value While existing literature mainly highlights the benefits of work-life integration, it rarely addresses the negative aspects, particularly in non-Western contexts. The empirical research explores both partial and sequential mediation of stress and satisfaction in this relationship.

title: Permission meets pressure: institutional risk, CEO self-monitoring and extreme strategic change
abstract: Purpose Explain why some multinationals pursue extreme strategic shifts whereas others opt for incremental change by testing how national institutions and CEO behavior interact. Design/methodology/approach We merge institutional-discretion theory with upper-echelons logic in a moderated-mediation model. Our sample has 1,422 firm-year observations (2000–2017) from US-based Fortune Global 500 firms operating abroad. Findings We find that institutional risk (societal tolerance for deviant action) heightens CEO self-monitoring, which in turn dampens the extremeness of strategic change. This indirect, risk-induced tempering effect is strongest in low-autonomy (tight) cultures where normative sanctions are salient and weakest in high-autonomy settings that relax conformity pressures. Research limitations/implications Future studies should treat managerial discretion as a cross-level paradox rather than a unidirectional catalyst. We encourage tests of the permission–pressure mechanism using other traits (e.g. political skill) and in contrasting institutional logics. Practical implications Boards and policy-makers should acknowledge that the same institutional features that grant executives more latitude can also make high self-monitors cautious. Aligning governance mechanisms with desired change magnitude requires tailoring incentives for high self-monitoring leaders or widening board expertise in tight cultures. Originality/value We introduce CEO self-monitoring as a conduit linking national discretion to change extremeness, enriching managerial-discretion theory. The study uncovers a novel permission–pressure paradox at the intersection of institutions and executive behavior.
